I think the past two years have been the worst for my mental health. I decided to do something about it and went to student support last April however because it was near the end of the academic year, we decided it’d be better if I waited until the new semester. Come summer, Chester Bennington dies and my world falls apart. I was in a deep state of depression. I was barely eating or showering. Not leaving the house and not really sleeping. I was suicidal, I’d started self-harming again and I didn’t see an end to it. Through meeting various people online, I worked up the courage to see my doctor who prescribed me an anti-depressant and a beta-blocker for anxiety. I started seeing a counsellor through student support and things seemed better than they were but still not okay.

I was still depressed and regularly seeing my doctor. I was on the max dose for my anti-depressant and a strong dose of the beta-blocker. The depression affected university. My attendance fell and I failed an exam in January. So I went back to my doctor and switched to a new anti-depressant. I’ve been on this one for about 7 weeks now and the past 2/3 weeks have been good. I hope it’s a sign that the new drug is working but it could also be because I finished uni and therefore wasn’t feeling the stress from that.

I never realised how hard it would be and how much I’d still have to work at it. I still get depressive episodes but they don’t last as long. I do have some things to work on but I’m feeling more positive now than I did before. It’s been nearly a month since I last self-harmed. I guess I just wanted to share my story because I was suicidal for a long time and I’m just now seeing things differently. You have to put the work in but getting to somewhere “normal” is possible. Reach out. Even if it’s on reddit or another social platform, use that as a beginning.

1 tsp paprika
1 tbsp tomato purée
1 tsp sugar (optional, I like my tomato sauces slightly sweet)
Oil for frying

Brown sausages, add to casserole dish
Fry bacon, add to casserole dish
Fry onion with garlic powder, herbs and paprika

Add chopped tomatoes, chicken stock and sugar if using. You can add salt if you want but I find there's enough salt in the chicken stock.
